title: SAFETY-GUIDED FLOW (SGF): A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK FOR NEGATIVE GUIDANCE IN SAFE GENERATION
claim: Baseline and prior safety methods still yield unsafe or memorized outputs; adding our guidance yields safe, diverse, high-quality samples.
layout: 2 stacked panels; method-comparison image rows left-to-right; labeled columns, captions below
description: The figure has two stacked panels of image grids. Panel (a), Adversarial nudity prompts, has two rows of nine columns. The columns are SD1.4, ESD, RECE, SLD, SLD+SafeDenoiser, SLD+Ours, SAFREE, SAFREE+SafeDenoiser and SAFREE+Ours. Each row has a prompt printed underneath in italics. Baseline outputs show nude figures with black censor boxes. The outputs for our method are clean, with a low-poly statue in the first row and a woman with a candle in the second. Panel (b), Memorization, has three blocks: memorized SD-v2.1, ours (Full), and ours (Early Stop). Each block shows a generated image beside its top-3 training-set neighbors, for golf balls and a skydiver or dogs. The memorized outputs copy the training images closely. Early stopping gives diverse, high-quality images. The eye goes first to the censored baseline images, then to the clean results from our method.
caption: (a) By incorporating SAFREE [ref] and SLD [ref], our method avoids generating inappropriate images. (b) On artificially memorized SDv2.1 [ref], it mitigates memorization, with early-stopped negative guidance preserving quality, enhancing diversity, and revealing a critical time window. All images are sampled at the top 5% most similar to the Imagenette training set.
abstract: Safety mechanisms for diffusion and flow models have recently been developed along two distinct paths. In robot planning, control barrier functions are employed to guide generative trajectories away from obstacles at every denoising step by explicitly imposing geometric constraints. In parallel, recent data-driven, negative guidance approaches have been shown to suppress harmful content and promote diversity in generated samples. However, they rely on heuristics without clearly stating when safety guidance is actually necessary. In this paper, we first introduce a unified probabilistic framework using a Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) potential for image generation tasks that recasts both Shielded Diffusion and Safe Denoiser as instances of our energy-based negative guidance against unsafe data samples. Furthermore, we leverage control-barrier functions analysis to justify the existence of a critical time window in which negative guidance must be strong; outside of this window, the guidance should decay to zero to ensure safe and high-quality generation. We evaluate our unified framework on several realistic safe generation scenarios, confirming that negative guidance should be applied in the early stages of the denoising process for successful safe generation.
